summary: Intermittent runtime heartbeat terminations causing elevated 5xxs during tenant concurrency ramp
description: Issue summary: Customers (notably BrightDoc AI on dedicated pool) observed a sudden elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway coinciding with a tenant concurrency ramp. Impact: sustained 5xx rate spike and streaming session drops causing degraded user experience for BrightDoc testing and several other tenants in the same dedicated cluster. Initial timeframe: 2026-03-13 11:15-12:40 UTC.
impact: Observed error rate climbed to 4.7% (baseline ~0.2%) for the affected pool. p95 request latency increased from 420ms to 1.8s. Multiple streaming sessions reset with grpc/HTTP2 RST. Customer reported timeouts and truncated responses during load testing. No data loss reported but degraded availability for traffic routed to the affected runtimes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightDoc AI tenant pinned to dedicated pool in prod-us-east.
2) Ramp concurrent streaming sessions from 50 to 600 over 10 minutes using the customer's harness (sustained ~50rps requests with long-filled token prefixes).
3) Observe API gateway logs for elevated 502/503 and runtime lifecycle events in runtime logs.
4) Reproduce consistently when repeat ramp executed within same pool configuration (seen in two separate runs).
logs: serving-runtime: 2026-03-13T11:22:12Z ERROR runtime: runtime process terminated exit_code=137 signal=SIGKILL
initial_hypothesis: Runtime heartbeat monitor is too aggressive during high prefetch/cache eviction jitter, causing processes to be terminated while still servicing requests.
Accept queue/backlog spike plus elevated FD usage temporarily delays heartbeat acknowledgements, triggering watchdog kills rather than graceful draining.
Autoscaler warmup/concurrency ramp created transient CPU scheduling pressure on the host, amplifying miss-detection.
Possibility of a recent runtime change to the heartbeat timeout or prefetch scheduling interacting poorly with tenant-heavy streaming workloads.
investigation_notes: 11:30 UTC - Support received first customer alert and validated elevated 502/503 counts in api-gateway metrics and observed corresponding runtime exits.
11:35 UTC - Correlated runtime 'missed_heartbeats' log entries with process OOM/kill (exit_code=137) in the same timestamp window; however memory footprints were within expected ranges for the model.
11:50 UTC - SRE reproduced the issue in a controlled ramp on a staging-like dedicated node. Observed ephemeral delay in event-loop scheduling and increased accept_queue_len prior to heartbeat misses.

12:10 UTC - Network stack metrics showed no packet loss between api-gateway and runtimes; TLS handshakes stable. CPU steal negligible on host, but user CPU and runqueue length spiked briefly during prefetch-heavy intervals.
12:25 UTC - Confirmed a recent configuration change (runtime heartbeat_grace_period reduced from 6s to 3s in canary two days ago) that made the monitor more sensitive. Rollback candidate identified.
12:40 UTC - Linked to prior incident SUP-720304 (autoscaler liveness loop) for similar tenant-burst amplification patterns; cross-referenced runbook.
mitigation_actions: 12:45 UTC - Temporarily increased heartbeat_grace_period to 8s via dynamic config for the affected dedicated pool to prevent further false-positive terminations.
12:55 UTC - Bumped accept queue size and tuned proxy keepalive timeout on the edge for the pool to reduce transient backlog pressure.
13:05 UTC - Applied autoscaler cooldown tweak to smooth rapid concurrency ramps for dedicated pools while permanent fix is prepared.
13:20 UTC - Customer BrightDoc AI notified of mitigations and asked to continue controlled verification tests; preliminary improvement observed (5xx rate dropped to 0.6% within 15 minutes).

SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-13T11:52Z: Reproduced locally. Seeing heartbeat misses preceding process kills. Suspect config sensitivity change rolled in last patch. Bringing down sensitivity as stopgap.

Customer (BrightDoc SRE - Elena Rossi) 2026-03-13T12:05Z: We are running the standard ramp test harness; happy to throttle ramps if needed. Observed same behavior on two separate runs within 20 minutes of each other.

Runtime Eng (Diego Morales) 2026-03-13T12:30Z: Noted PR #4820 adjusted heartbeat behavior for faster failure detection. We'll evaluate tradeoffs and propose a fix to avoid terminations during transient scheduling stalls.

resolution: Temporary: Restored heartbeat_grace_period to 8s for affected pool and adjusted accept queue sizing; autoscaler cooldown increased to reduce ramp velocity.
Permanent: Engineering to revert the aggressive heartbeat change in runtime or implement jitter-tolerant ack logic. Patch PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4832
Follow-up task: INT-2287 created to add additional telemetry around heartbeat ack latencies, accept-queue depth, and prefetch eviction stalls for future correlation.
Customer communication: Full incident summary and mitigation timeline sent to BrightDoc support contact.
